Optimization and Regularization01

An iterative method

Instead of jumping straight to the bottom of the bowl, we can walk downhill a little at a time.

w \leftarrow \lk{step}{w - \lk{alpha}{\alpha}\,\lk{grad}{\frac{\partial L}{\partial w}}}
Optimization and Regularization · Optimization03

Overfitting

Unfortunately, Linear Regressions (a form of MLE), are prone to overfitting.

Optimization and Regularization · Optimization05

Regularization: L1 and L2

To help prevent overfitting when using linear regressions, we can perform a technique called regularization.

The goal of regularization is to encourage models to learn the broader patterns within the data rather than memorizing it.

L2 regularization: Ridge

L2 regularization (called ridge regularization) encourages small (but nonzero) weights.

L1 regularization: LASSO

L1 regularization (also called LASSO) leads to weights of exactly zero and sparse models.

Optimization and Regularization · Regularization06

Formalizations of regularization

There are two ways to formalize regularization:

  • As a cost (penalty) placed on the weights
  • As a budget (constraint) for the weights
Optimization and Regularization · Regularization08

Regularization as a cost

When we formalize regularization as a cost, we modify the loss function such that increasing the weights incurs a "cost".

We use an argument called λ to determine how heavily the cost is weighed. A larger λ increases the cost.

L(w) = \text{SSE}(w) + \lambda \sum_j w_j^2 L(w) = \text{SSE}(w) + \lambda \sum_j |w_j|
Optimization and Regularization · Regularization09

Regularization as a cost, increasing λ

A larger λ increases the cost of our weights, typically resulting in the optimum being pulled closer to the origin.

Optimization and Regularization · Regularization11

Regularization as a budget

When we formalize regularization as a budget, we constrain our loss function such that the weights chosen must remain within "budget".

\min_w \ \text{SSE}(w) \quad \text{subject to} \quad \sum_j w_j^2 \le t \min_w \ \text{SSE}(w) \quad \text{subject to} \quad \sum_j |w_j| \le t
Optimization and Regularization · Regularization12

Regularization as a budget, increasing t

A larger t increases the budget for our weights, typically resulting in the optimum being closer to the unconstrained optimum.

Optimization and Regularization · Regularization13

MAP estimation

L1 and L2 regularization are a form of MAP Estimation.

MAP stands for Maximum A Posteriori which is a Bayesian approach for applying a prior to our weights.

Optimization and Regularization · Regularization20

Review

Complete the review: L1 regularization penalizes the absolute values of the weights. L2 regularization penalizes the squared weights. In a penalty formulation, increasing lambda makes the penalty stronger. In a budget formulation, increasing the budget makes the constraint looser.
